title: Homemade guitar picks and drummer Charlie Blue Watson
summary: Players cut picks from combs and corset stays; Julius's cousin Charlie Watson drummed for his father.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well, at that time, the guitar players used to take the regular combs, you know, that the ladies used to comb their hair with. Well, they had this part, it was about that wide before the comb part. Right. And they used to take a file or a knife and shave it down and then, you know, make picks out of it.

Well, I imagine so. But, I mean, it was just, it weren't, they didn't do anything, I mean, they didn't have picks that you could buy at that time. You couldn't buy that because I remember, it's funny, my mother didn't wear corsets, but so many of them that, war corsets, and they'd wear out. We'd be running to find the well-borne in it. You understand what I mean?
We'd be running to find that in it.

And, so, some of them wouldn't have the well-borne, they'd have that little, we used to call it iron, it wasn't iron, no, it was that thin thin steel like the well-borne in it. But, man, when we'd find that well-borne, oh shoot, we had pitched the last of the house. Took a free year. Yeah. But, we had, now they had a cousin of mine who used to play drums with my dad. His name was Charlie Blue, Charlie Watson was his name, we used to call him Charlie Blue. Oh, he was a great drummer, he was great. And, well, he was a good baseball player, he used to play baseball too. And, I don't know when it happened that he quit playing with my daddy.
